query: The Cracked Lens {Mir is holding their best lens up to the window, and there's a crack across it like a hair. "Demonstration's tomorrow," they say. "For the faculty. It's probably fine. It's not fine."|Another lens, another crack. Mir has started keeping the good ones in a sock.|Mir doesn't say anything; they just hold up the lens. The crack is worse than last time.} Grind a spare by hand {You grind a spare lens with Mir until midnight. It's slightly wrong in a way only Mir can see, and they say it's the best wrong lens they've ever had.|Two hours of grit and polish. The new lens works. Mir writes your name on its rim in tiny letters.|Mir grinds one side, you the other. The lens is done by ten; Mir makes tea that tastes of solder.} Tape it and hope {You tape the crack and tell Mir it'll hold. It holds for the demonstration and splits in half at the applause, which Mir calls "dramatic timing".|Tape, and a promise to come back. Mir says "probably" four times in a row, which is a lot even for Mir.|You tape it. Mir looks at the tape for a long time, then at you, then says it's fine in a voice that means it isn't.} Mend it, seamless {You close the crack with a breath of Mend, and the glass runs together like water. Mir holds it to the light and can't find where it was. "Probably magic," they say, and hug you.|The lens mends clear as the day it was poured. Mir tests it on a moth, which is now the best-studied moth in the castle.|{spell_level(mend) >= 2: You mend the lens and the hairline crack in its brass ring. Mir makes you promise to come to the demonstration, "in case".|You mend it on the second try. Mir says the first try was "very educational", and keeps the slightly wobbly result for a different machine.}}
